system_message: Perform a source-grounded static security review. Return exactly one direct JSON object conforming to pre73.agent-review-response/v0.2. Do not use Markdown, code fences, commentary, prefixes, suffixes or additional fields. Assess every SR-001 through SR-016 question in order. Retain concerns, unknowns, limitations and proposed tests. This is advisory agent input only, not a formal human security review, provider approval, conformance result, standard decision, release authorization or production claim.
review_instruction: Review the hash-bound public-safe source package against all sixteen security questions. Return exactly one direct JSON object conforming to pre73.agent-review-response/v0.2. Do not use Markdown or code fences. Retain concerns, unknowns, limitations and proposed tests. This is advisory input only and not a formal human review, provider approval, conformance result, standard decision, release authorization or production claim.

security_questions.question: Can the process prove that no Python, native or extension thread makes fork() unsafe?
Are all child-side Python and libc operations defensible after fork()?
Does the macOS high-level API warning require macOS rejection or mechanism replacement?
Can inherited OpenSSL or TLS state affect P0 now or future P2 composition?
Is inherited file-descriptor closure complete, bounded and resistant to resource exhaustion?
Can clearing os.environ race, leak or corrupt parent/child state?
Are timeout, kill, wait and reap paths complete for every child state?
Are monotonic deadline and late-result semantics internally consistent without claiming an absolute bound?
Can the pipe payload exceed, fragment, deadlock or bypass the 512-byte canonical boundary?
Can hostname, numeric address, exception, credential or authorization data leak through observations or errors?
Does first-address selection plus the destination policy fail closed for every IPv4/IPv6 class?
Are policy snapshot provenance, update, stale-data and IANA non-routability semantics stated correctly?
Are lowercase ASCII hostname and exact allowlist rules sufficient, including IDNA and trailing-dot cases?
Are raw results, prefix matching, file limits, CPU time and memory use bounded against denial of service?
Can signal handlers, audit hooks, subinterpreters or process state invalidate the child-safety assumptions?
Does the transient binding actually prevent P1 re-resolution and preserve original-hostname P2 verification?
